title: Slide a wood stove's flue damper open
instruction: Slide the wood stove's flue damper open.
context: A damper left closed fills the room with smoke on the first fire of the season, and the damper's position is invisible from outside the firebox - the operator slides the gate aside and judges the opening by eye. It is the one wood-stove check homeowners most often get wrong.
setup: All rigid boxes on the station table (scene 'station', table top at 75 cm). A wood stove body 20x16x18 cm, grey cast-iron, centred at (37, -16) cm with its base on the table. Its top plate is four steel-grey strips 1.5 cm thick on the body's top, framing a 6 cm square flue opening centred at (37, -16) cm: left and right strips 7x16x1.5 cm spanning x 27-34 and 40-47 cm, front and back strips 6x5x1.5 cm at y -21.5 and -10.5 cm. The slide-gate damper, a polished-steel plate 7.8x9.4x2.5 cm, 0.6 kg, lies flat on the strips' top centred at (37, -16) cm, rest + 17.75 cm, covering the flue opening with 0.9 cm of bearing per side.
scoring: Scored at the episode end with the gate at rest (speeds under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s): 1.0 when the gate's centre has moved at least 7.5 cm from its closed position (x 37 cm) and its centre height is within 2 cm of riding height (rest + 17.75 cm) - the flue stands uncovered; 0.5 for a 3.5-7.5 cm move (the flue partly exposed); 0.0 closed, fallen to the table, or carried off the stove's top. Do-nothing: 0 - the closed gate is a stable flat spawn and cannot uncover the flue on its own.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed; the gate spawns closed, centred on the flue opening, in one fixed layout.
fidelity: A rigid-body stand-in at bench scale. The gate is a real free plate sliding on the stove's top strips: closed it bridges the opening, displaced it rests flat on the same surface. The gate's mass is set to 0.6 kg (a real 2.5 cm cast-iron plate this size is ~1.5 kg; the reduction keeps the carry inside the jaw's hold budget), and its finish is rendered as polished steel so the plate reads clearly on the dark stove top. The flue is a framed opening rather than a piped stack, and the smoke path is not simulated - the gate's displacement off the opening is exactly what a tape measure and a photo check.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2400 steps, hit the step limit; the policy held its home pose throughout and never approached the stove); scripted demo: 1.0
